# IMDb.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/imdb-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/imdb-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects data from IMDb.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape IMDb Data, Ratings, and Featured Reviews](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-imdb)
- **Code:** [`imdb.py`](imdb.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Chart](results/chart.json) · [Person](results/person.json) · [Reviews](results/reviews.json) · [Search](results/search.json) · [Title](results/title.json)

## What it scrapes

- IMDb title pages for movie/TV metadata
- IMDb review pages for user reviews
- IMDb search pages for title search results
- IMDb chart pages (e.g. Top 250)
- IMDb person pages for biography and filmography

## Functions

- `scrape_titles(urls)` → `List[IMDbTitle]`: scrape IMDb title pages for metadata and aggregate ratings
- `scrape_reviews(title_id)` → `List[IMDbReview]`: scrape user reviews from the title reviews page hidden dataset
- `scrape_search(query)` → `List[IMDbSearchResult]`: scrape IMDb title search results for a query
- `scrape_chart(chart_type='top')` → `List[IMDbChartEntry]`: scrape an IMDb chart (e.g. 'top' for Top 250)
- `scrape_person(person_id)` → `IMDbPerson`: scrape an IMDb person page for biography and filmography

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import imdb


async def main():
    titles = await imdb.scrape_titles(urls=["https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0111161/"])
    reviews = await imdb.scrape_reviews(title_id="tt0111161")
    search = await imdb.scrape_search(query="shawshank")
    chart = await imdb.scrape_chart(chart_type="top")
    person = await imdb.scrape_person(person_id="nm0000209")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`IMDbReview`**: `id`, `author?`, `summary?`, `text?`, `rating?`, `spoiler`
- **`IMDbTitle`**: `id`, `url`, `name`, `type?`, `rating_value?`, `rating_count?`, `content_rating?`, `genre?`, `description?`, `cast?`, `directors?`, `runtime_minutes?`, `keywords?`, `box_office?`, `release_date?`
- **`IMDbSearchResult`**: `id`, `url`, `name?`, `type?`, `year?`, `rating_value?`, `rating_count?`
- **`IMDbChartEntry`**: `rank?`, `id`, `url`, `name?`, `type?`, `rating_value?`, `rating_count?`, `year?`
- **`IMDbPerson`**: `id?`, `url`, `name?`, `bio?`, `birth_date?`, `professions?`, `filmography?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`imdb.py`](imdb.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/imdb-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_title_scraping`, `test_review_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_chart_scraping`, `test_person_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
